findings.what: ADR-038 §f still read 'measured sound on all 18 here' — byte-identical to the pre-repair line at 3ed9003 — while :12, :736 and the row directly above said 17/14. Round 1's sweep pattern ('18/6|18 items across 6|18 across 6|...') could not match a bare 'all 18 here', so the resolution's 'no stale count survives anywhere' was reported clean over a surviving one.
findings.fix: The line now reads 'measured sound on all 17 in-class items here'. The sweep is re-run with a pattern that matches a BARE number adjacent to any census/count word in either order, over nine surfaces including the instrument script; it now reports its filter's UNPIPED exit code rather than a pipe's.
findings.self_criticism: A sweep whose pattern is narrower than its claim is the same defect class as a check that cannot fail. Round 1's sweep asserted a universal ('no stale claim survives anywhere') from a finite literal list — the assertion should have been scoped to what the pattern could see, or the pattern widened to match the assertion. The widened sweep then caught a FOURTH surface for R10 that R10 itself did not name (prompts/024:65).

findings.disposition: REPAIRED — the argument is weakened to a true one
findings.what: (a) The published intc-2002 figure was 110; it is 111 — a retyped number, wrong, in a section arguing figures must be derived, in the same PR where a retyped number was already wrong once. (b) 'Measured the same way' was false for exactly the load-bearing item: --prong1 segments intc-2002 item 5 as [0] 201 / [1] 359 / [2] 5, with the holder sentence INSIDE [1] together with a pointer clause, while ba-2003's 74/145/89 and textron-2001's 104/86 ARE splitter sentences. The 111 was an undisclosed hand sub-split. (c) Consequently 'no threshold separates them' held only under that split. (d) --prong1's output was neither committed nor listed in Verification, which is exactly why the off-by-one survived.
findings.fix_instrument: --prong1 now carries a printed NON_POINTER map (hand-marked, movable, same convention as the anchors), asserts its hand sub-split string is actually in the body, and prints the threshold comparison under BOTH readings. Its output is committed at tasks/reviews/d13-prong1.txt and listed in ADR-038's Verification beside --table and --auditor-input. Every figure R10 disputes — 111, 176, 190, 308, 359 and the 177..190 interval — is now derived by that script, not retyped.
findings.fix_prose: §e3's threshold paragraph is rewritten. It states the hand sub-split explicitly ('the instrument does NOT split this'), publishes BOTH readings in a table, and concedes that under the instrument's own segmentation the three rejections span 190..359 so a threshold in 177..190 DOES separate them from xom item 8's 176.
findings.does_the_conclusion_survive: YES, but on a weaker and true ground. The length reading is now REFUSED, not refuted, on three grounds independent of the split: (1) a threshold in 177..190 is fitted to four bodies with a 13-char margin, which is not a band — ADR-007's own comment refuses to move a constant no case can distinguish, and ADR-030/ADR-035 pin both edges of a measured band before adopting one; (2) the figure it would key on flips on a sub-sentence judgement (111 vs 359 for the same body), and a discriminator that unstable is worse than none; (3) the kind test needs no constant and the reviewer independently re-derived that it sorts all 17 in-class bodies consistently. §f's reopener is sharpened to 'exhibit a body the kind test mis-sorts'.
